i: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
su: A one-year non-ACGME fellowship at one of the top U.S. transplant centres providing comprehensive perioperative training for adult abdominal organ transplant recipients plus complex hepatobiliary, vascular and cardiothoracic surgery.

f.International applicants: Institution policy: International graduates accepted via ECFMG J-1 sponsorship (H-1B at programme discretion); Missouri temporary licence requires a permanent ECFMG certificate
f.Visa support: Unable to support any visa sponsorship at this time
f.Funding: Institution policy: WashU/BJH/SLCH GME Consortium stipends 1 July 2026-30 June 2027: PGY1 $71,239; PGY2 $74,399; PGY3 $77,597; PGY4 $80,895; PGY5 $84,439; PGY6 $88,091; PGY7 $91,618; PGY8 $95,032; PGY9 $99,151 (all fellows paid PGY-based salary whether or not ACGME-accredited)

i: Toronto General Hospital (University Health Network)
su: Focuses on liver transplantation and major abdominal surgical oncology anaesthesia at the largest transplant centre in Canada.

f.Deadline: Applications open 24 months and close 12 months before the intended start date
f.International applicants: Yes — applicants trained in countries where English is not the primary language must demonstrate effective communication in English
f.Visa support: Institution policy: international clinical fellows need an IRCC work permit; the PGME Office issues an LMIA-exempt offer of employment number and supports the work permit application
f.Funding: Institution policy: clinical fellows must be funded (department or sponsoring agency); FEAC recommends pay at least equal to PGY1 on the PARO salary scale, and foreign nationals must be paid at a rate commensurate with a Canadian in the same role
f.Start: Normally beginning of February and beginning of August each year

i: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
o: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
su: Fellows assess transplant candidates and living donors and provide anaesthesia for kidney, pancreas, islet, intestinal, multivisceral and uterine transplants at the Oxford Transplant Centre.

f.International applicants: Yes — international doctors may be appointed via the Medical Training Initiative (MTI) or a Skilled Worker (Tier 2) Certificate of Sponsorship
f.Visa support: MTI route: RCoA-sponsored GMC registration and Tier 5 visa via Academy of Medical Royal Colleges CoS; alternatively Skilled Worker (Tier 2) CoS assigned by OUH
f.Funding: Not stated on official page

t: Adult and Pediatric Pain Medicine Dual Fellowship
i: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
su: A combined pain medicine fellowship training consultants to manage acute and chronic pain from neonates to the elderly through roughly six months each of pediatric and adult curricula.

f.Duration: About 6 months pediatric and 6 months adult curriculum
f.International applicants: Institution policy: International graduates accepted via ECFMG J-1 sponsorship (H-1B at programme discretion); Missouri temporary licence requires a permanent ECFMG certificate
f.Visa support: Institution policy: WashU GME Consortium supports ECFMG J-1 visas (managed by institutional Training Program Liaisons); H-1B may be supported at department/programme discretion; WashU holds ACGME Non-Standard Training recognition so non-accredited fellowships can host J-1 trainees
f.Funding: Stipend per WashU GME scale (e.g. PGY5 $84,439)

i: McGill University
su: A one-year clinical fellowship in adult cardiac anaesthesia within the McGill Department of Anesthesia.

f.Deadline: 2027–2028 applications opened 15 May 2026; deadline for most fellowships 1 September 2026 (see PGME Application Timelines)
f.International applicants: Yes — Regular Track positions open to Canadian and international applicants; French language training mandatory for fellows with no or limited conversational French
f.Visa support: Not stated on official page
f.Funding: Candidates must secure funding in order to apply; self-funding not accepted; Quebec-trained residents may apply for RAMQ-funded fellowships

i: Baylor College of Medicine
o: Baylor College of Medicine / Texas Children's
su: A year-long ACGME fellowship at the Texas Heart Institute/Baylor St. Luke's specialising in adult cardiac, thoracic, vascular and transplant anesthesia, with electives in cardiology, perfusion and congenital heart surgery at Texas Children's.

f.International applicants: Institution policy: IMGs welcomed and encouraged to apply; ECFMG certification required (except Canadian graduates); must secure an appropriate visa and Texas Medical Board permit
f.Visa support: Institution policy: Visa types sponsored vary by department (check with the programme); IMGs must secure an appropriate visa
f.Funding: Institution policy: Paid on BCM 2026-27 stipend scale: PGY4 $79,450, PGY5 $83,325, PGY6 $86,025, PGY7 $88,926, PGY8 $91,150

i: Massachusetts General Hospital
su: Cardiothoracic anesthesia training includes complex cardiac procedures, dedicated echocardiography, thoracic surgery and cardiovascular ICU care.

f.Deadline: 2027-28: programme deadline 31 January 2026 (SF Match target 4 March 2026; registration opened 3 November 2025). Next cycle (integrated MGB, July 2028 start): SF Match registration opens 2 November 2026, application deadline 30 March 2027, match results 17 June 2027
f.International applicants: Yes - IMGs with the credentials listed on the official page; non-US citizens/permanent residents must hold an appropriate visa
f.Visa support: Mass General Brigham sponsors H-1B and J-1 visas for eligible applicants
f.Funding: Paid at PGY-5 level; starting PGY-5 salary in 2026 is $102,466
f.Start: 2027-28 academic year is the final MGH cohort; from 1 July 2028 training is in the merged MGB Adult Cardiothoracic Anesthesia Fellowship

i: Vanderbilt University Medical Center
su: Clinical training spans cardiac surgery, heart and lung transplantation, structural-heart procedures, thoracic anesthesia and mechanical circulatory support.

f.Deadline: Applications via SF Match accepted from November through 31 January
f.International applicants: Institutional GME requirement: holders of a foreign medical degree need a valid ECFMG certificate; no programme-specific policy stated
f.Visa support: Institution policy: J-1 via ECFMG; H-1B considered case by case by programme with GME; no new O-1 applications supported
f.Funding: Salary not stated; CME budget provided for conference attendance

i: University of Michigan
su: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship providing advanced training in the preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative care of adults undergoing cardiac, thoracic and intrathoracic vascular surgery, with comprehensive advanced perioperative TEE training at the Frankel Cardiovascular Center.

f.Duration: One year (12 months of clinical rotations)
f.International applicants: Institution policy: Yes - non-US medical graduates must hold a current ECFMG certificate and be eligible for a State of Michigan licence; non-US citizens need ECFMG J-1, permanent residence or qualifying EAD
f.Visa support: Institution policy: J-1 sponsored by ECFMG (or permanent residence / qualifying EAD); other visas only in very limited circumstances, case by case at Program Director discretion with prospective GME Committee approval
f.Funding: Salary commensurate with a House Officer at an equivalent level of training (HOA contract)

i: Cleveland Clinic
su: Established in 1976, Cleveland Clinic's ACGME-accredited adult cardiothoracic anesthesiology fellowship is the largest in the U.S., offering a high volume of complex, high-acuity cardiac, thoracic and vascular cases.

f.International applicants: ECFMG certificate required if applicable; J-1 visa holders referenced
f.Visa support: J-1 referenced (start date accommodation); other visa types not stated
f.Funding: Not stated on official page
f.Start: August 1 (July 1 if required by military service or for J-1 visa holders)

i: Columbia University Irving Medical Center
su: Training spans cardiac and thoracic operations, mechanical circulatory support, and heart and lung transplantation, with progressive responsibility as the primary anesthesia provider.

f.Deadline: 4 January 2027 (complete SF Match application); interviews February-April 2027; rank list deadline 3 June 2027
f.International applicants: Foreign nationals generally accepted only with ECFMG-sponsored J-1 status (O-1 in very limited cases; no H-1); ACGME-accredited anesthesiology residency required
f.Visa support: Generally J-1 through ECFMG; O-1 support in very limited circumstances. The page explicitly excludes H-1 sponsorship.
f.Funding: Salary not stated on programme page; fellows receive an educational stipend plus time and financial support for regional/national conferences
f.Start: July/August 2028 for the 2026-2027 SF Match cycle (flexible start dates, schedule permitting)

i: Duke University
su: Training covers complex cardiac and thoracic surgery, echocardiography, perfusion and cardiothoracic intensive care.

f.Duration: 12 months; an individualized second clinical or research year may be available
f.Deadline: 3 March 2027 for the 2028-29 fellowship (SF Match registration opens 2 November 2026; applications accepted on a rolling basis from November 2026)
f.International applicants: Institution policy: Yes - graduates of medical schools outside the US/Canada are eligible if they hold a valid ECFMG certificate or a full unrestricted US licence
f.Visa support: Institution policy: J-1 alien physician status sponsored by ECFMG with Duke's assistance; Duke is H-1B cap-exempt and H-1B is possible for clinical trainees who have passed USMLE Steps 1-3 and hold an ECFMG certificate (individual programmes decide which visas they accept)
f.Funding: Institution policy: GME trainees paid on the Duke stipend scale; FY27 (from 1 July 2026) PGY-1 $71,052 rising to PGY-4 $79,908, PGY-5 $82,992, PGY-6 $86,292, PGY-7 $90,036 (up to PGY-12 $106,800), plus benefits

i: Emory University School of Medicine
su: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship preparing graduates for independent practice in adult cardiothoracic anesthesiology and NBE advanced perioperative TEE certification.

f.Deadline: SF Match; applications accepted from about 18 months before the start date, interviews March-May
f.International applicants: Institution policy: International medical graduates eligible if ECFMG-certified and holding J-1 (ECFMG) or H-1B status, or US citizen/permanent resident
f.Visa support: Institution policy: IMGs must be ECFMG-certified and enter training on a J-1 (ECFMG-sponsored) or H-1B visa unless US citizen/green-card holder (Emory GME housestaff policy 5.12)
f.Funding: Institution policy: Salaried by Emory GME on uniform PGY scale (1 Jul 2026-30 Jun 2027): PGY4 $81,720; PGY5 $85,455; PGY6 $87,023; PGY7 $88,522; PGY8 $90,831 (PGY1 $71,959)
f.Start: Institution policy: Emory house staff appointments typically cover a 1 July - 30 June academic year (standard start 1 July)

i: Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine (McGaw Medical Center)
su: An ACGME-accredited year of clinical, educational and academic training at the Bluhm Cardiovascular Institute within Northwestern Memorial Hospital, including more than 600 non-cardiac thoracic cases a year.

f.International applicants: Institution policy: IMGs eligible with a valid ECFMG certificate, valid visa (J-1, H-1B or O-1) or permanent residence, and Illinois IDFPR licence
f.Visa support: Institution policy: McGaw sponsors J-1 (ECFMG) and supports H-1B only for exceptional candidates approved by the DIO/GMEC before ranking (cost borne by programme)
f.Funding: Paid internal weekend moonlighting permitted after the first three months

i: Stanford Medicine
su: Cardiothoracic operating-room and cardiovascular ICU training with dedicated echocardiography, transplant and mechanical-support experience.

f.Deadline: 1 February 2027; applications accepted 2 November 2026 - 1 February 2027 (interviews March 2027; rank lists due 3 June 2027; match results 17 June 2027)
f.International applicants: International medical graduates should contact the programme directly about eligibility
f.Visa support: Not stated on official page
f.Funding: Paid GME position on the Stanford Health Care housestaff salary scale (e.g. PGY-5 $119,558.40/yr on current posted scale); plus one-time $3,600 departmental housing stipend, $1,000 education fund, sponsored SCA Echo Week/Annual Meeting attendance (up to $6,500)

i: UCLA Health
su: Cardiothoracic training combining operating-room care, advanced echocardiography and cardiothoracic intensive care, including transplant and mechanical-support cases.

f.Deadline: Application submission period November through January via SF Match (2027-2028 intake opened November 2025); interviews in March
f.International applicants: IMGs may apply; valid ECFMG certificate and notarized English translations of diploma/transcripts required
f.Visa support: Not stated on official page
f.Funding: Not stated on official page

i: UCSF Health
su: An ACGME-accredited programme focused on perioperative care for complex cardiac and thoracic surgery, transplantation, mechanical support and advanced cardiovascular procedures.

f.International applicants: Institution policy: IMGs eligible if their school is in the World Directory/FAIMER and they hold a valid ECFMG certificate at application; non-US citizens need permanent residence, an appropriate visa or DACA
f.Visa support: Institution policy: UCSF sponsors J-1 (ECFMG) and H-1B (incl. OPT) visas; H-1B/OPT require pre-approval by UCSF OGME; non-ACGME fellowships can take J-1 trainees only if ACGME Non-Standard Training (NST) recognised
f.Funding: Institution policy: Salaried on UCSF CIR collective-bargaining scale (rates effective 1 Oct 2025, incl. housing allowance): PGY4 $106,127; PGY5 $109,737; PGY6 $113,149; PGY7 $116,315; PGY8 $121,494; 2026-27 scale under union negotiation

i: University of Pennsylvania (Penn Medicine)

f.Duration: One year (two-year combined CCM/ACTA track available)
f.Deadline: Applications accepted from January 1 to March 31 of the year before the start date
f.International applicants: Not stated on official page
f.Visa support: Not stated on official page
f.Funding: Institution policy: UPHS housestaff (CIR union) scale effective 1 Oct 2026: PGY4 $90,390.74, PGY5 $93,463.38, PGY6 $97,394.78, PGY7 $100,083.62, plus $11,000 annual stipend for all PGYs

i: University of Pittsburgh / UPMC

f.Funding: Institution policy: Salaried on UPMC ME GMT stipend scale AY 2026-27: PGY4 $78,677; PGY5 $81,431; PGY6 $84,281; PGY7 $87,231; PGY8 $90,284 (AY 2027-28: PGY4 $81,818; PGY5 $85,091; PGY6 $88,495)

i: University of Washington

f.Visa support: Institution policy: J-1 sponsored by ECFMG (ACGME programmes and non-ACGME programmes approved as ACGME non-standard training); H-1B only with prior GME Office (and ISO) approval before ranking/offer, for limited eligibility categories and requires USMLE Step 3; F-1 OPT accepted; no O-1 or permanent-residence sponsorship
f.Funding: Salary per UW GME schedule; academic allowance subject to available funding
f.Start: Institution policy: UW GME academic year runs 1 July - 30 June (standard start 1 July)

i: UT Southwestern Medical Center

f.Visa support: Institution policy: Clinical residents/fellows (ACGME and non-ACGME) on J-1 sponsored by ECFMG; UTSW does not usually sponsor H-1B for clinical training
f.Funding: Institution policy: Paid house-staff stipend (employer varies: UTSW, Parkland, Children's Health or Scottish Rite); 2026-27 scale PGY4 $82,225, PGY5 $86,343, PGY6 $89,505, PGY7 $95,050

i: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
su: A flexible ACGME fellowship developing expert-level skills in cardiac and thoracic surgical anesthesia, with protected TEE time toward NBE Advanced PTEeXAM certification and a CTICU rotation in a 27-bed unit.

f.Visa support: Institution policy: WashU GME Consortium supports ECFMG J-1 visas (managed by institutional Training Program Liaisons); H-1B may be supported at department/programme discretion; WashU holds ACGME Non-Standard Training recognition so non-accredited fellowships can host J-1 trainees
f.Funding: Stipend per WashU GME scale (e.g. PGY5 $84,439); discretionary fund for books and training expenses

i: Weill Cornell Medicine / NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital
su: A 12-month ACGME-accredited fellowship (established 1989) at NewYork-Presbyterian/Weill Cornell training cardiothoracic anesthesiologists expert in perioperative medicine and echocardiography; a two-year combined option with critical care is available.

f.International applicants: Institution policy: Foreign nationals accepted only if they secure ECFMG J-1 status or hold work authorization for the programme duration; IMGs need ECFMG certification
f.Visa support: NewYork-Presbyterian accepts only J-1 visas for ACGME fellowship programmes in the Department of Anesthesiology
f.Funding: Institution policy: NYPH 2026-27 GME salary: PGY4 $119,100, PGY5 $123,000, PGY6 $125,200, PGY7 $129,100, plus $7,500 living supplement, $1,000 academic stipend, Lyft and meal credits
f.Start: Institution policy: NYP graduate staff appointment year is generally 1 July - 30 June

i: Mayo Clinic — Minnesota
su: Cardiac, thoracic and major vascular anesthesia training offers individualized experience in echocardiography, research and simulation.

f.Deadline: 31 March of the year preceding programme start
f.International applicants: Not stated on official page
f.Visa support: J-1 via ECFMG sponsorship; Mayo Clinic may also sponsor H-1B if all eligibility requirements are met
f.Funding: Paid; Mayo Clinic GME stipend by graduate level (effective 11 March 2026: e.g. Graduate Level 5 $89,036/yr); benefits include 20 working days' vacation

t: Adult Cardiovascular Anesthesia and Intensive Care Fellowship

i: Toronto General Hospital (University Health Network)

f.Funding: Institution policy: clinical fellows must be funded (department or sponsoring agency); FEAC recommends pay at least equal to PGY1 on the PARO salary scale, and foreign nationals must be paid at a rate commensurate with a Canadian in the same role

t: Adult Critical Care Fellowship (Anesthesiology Critical Care Medicine)

f.Visa support: Institution policy: Johns Hopkins SOM sponsors incoming residents/fellows for J-1 (ECFMG); H-1B only in limited cases (US MD graduates on OPT in ACGME training, or trainees already on H-1B in ACGME-accredited/recognised training with sufficient H-1B time remaining) - GME policy P&F028

i: Toronto General Hospital (University Health Network)
su: Focuses on acquiring expertise in airway evaluation and management, including care of patients undergoing complex head and neck surgery, so the fellow can serve as a resource in teaching and managing difficult airways.

su: Individualised advanced experience across difficult airway, thoracic, neuro, high-risk obstetric, regional, transplant, bariatric and paediatric anaesthesia.

f.Visa support: Institution policy: J-1 (ECFMG) is the primary visa; H-1B permitted only in some circumstances with GME approval; O-1 rarely, varies by department

f.International applicants: Institution policy: IMGs welcome to apply; must hold a valid ECFMG certificate and be able to obtain Medical Board of California licensure; non-ACGME fellowships need ACGME Non-Standard Training recognition before J-1 sponsorship

su: A salaried advanced clinical fellowship at Sunnybrook with formal evaluation at 6 and 12 months and a completion certificate.

f.International applicants: Yes — open to international graduates; applicants whose first language is not English must pass TOEFL/TSE or IELTS

su: Broad clinical anaesthesia experience including neuro and spine surgery at Toronto Western and ambulatory day-surgery anaesthesia at Women's College Hospital.

f.Visa support: Not stated on official page

su: An advanced training opportunity for early or mid-career physicians to develop as medical education leaders through a keystone medical education project, 12 hours per week of clinical work in the Stanford operating rooms, and access to Stanford teaching and simulation programmes.

su: A 12-month ACGME-accredited fellowship that has trained more than 200 fellows since 1987, based at the HSS main campus, ambulatory surgery centres, Sports Medicine Institute and Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center.

f.Duration: 1 year (12 months); starts after ABA board exams in August
f.Positions: 11 (for graduates of accredited anesthesiology residency programmes)
f.International applicants: Non-US citizens accepted if they maintain appropriate immigration status (ECFMG J-1)
f.Visa support: Non-US citizens apply for ECFMG J-1 visa sponsorship; non-US citizens may work on a New York State limited permit
f.Funding: Stipend $109,900 per annum plus benefits

t: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship
i: Massachusetts General Hospital
su: Regional and acute pain training covers adult and pediatric techniques, inpatient consultation and ambulatory catheter care.

f.Deadline: 2027-28: SF Match registration opened 5 January 2026, deadline 10 May 2026. Next cycle: integrated MGB RAPM fellowship (2028-29) via SF Match - see SF Match calendar
f.Positions: 2 per year (MGH programme); integrated MGB programme offers 6 positions per year from 2028
f.International applicants: Yes - non-LCME/AOA graduates eligible with applicable USMLE requirements; ACGME-accredited anesthesiology residency required (integrated programme criteria)
f.Visa support: Mass General Brigham sponsors H-1B and J-1 visas for eligible applicants
f.Funding: Paid at PGY-5 level; starting PGY-5 salary in 2026 is $102,466
f.Start: 1 July 2027 (final MGH cohort); integrated MGB programme from July 2028

t: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship
i: Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine (McGaw Medical Center)
su: An ACGME-accredited 12-month fellowship shared between Northwestern Memorial Hospital (9 months) and Lurie Children’s Hospital (3 months).

f.International applicants: Institution policy: IMGs eligible with a valid ECFMG certificate, valid visa (J-1, H-1B or O-1) or permanent residence, and Illinois IDFPR licence
f.Visa support: Institution policy: McGaw sponsors J-1 (ECFMG) and supports H-1B only for exceptional candidates approved by the DIO/GMEC before ranking (cost borne by programme)
f.Funding: Institution policy: Paid on McGaw salary scale 2026-27: PGY4 $89,096.50, PGY5 $92,697.20, PGY6 $95,567.99, PGY7+ $99,276.90

t: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship
i: NYU Langone Health (NYU Grossman School of Medicine)
su: A one-year ACGME-accredited programme training physicians to employ regional anesthesiology techniques, with rotations at an ambulatory orthopaedic surgical centre, Tisch Hospital and Hassenfeld Children’s Hospital.

f.International applicants: Institution policy: International graduates may train on an ECFMG-sponsored J-1 visa only (no H-1B); non-accredited fellowships require a NY licence or limited permit
f.Visa support: Institution policy: NYU Langone does not offer H-1B sponsorship for residents or fellows; J-1 sponsorship available through ECFMG
f.Funding: Not stated on official page

t: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship
i: Stanford Medicine
su: Advanced regional anaesthesia and acute pain training with a broad clinical case mix and academic development opportunities.

f.Deadline: SF Match: 2026 cycle applications opened 1 January 2026, deadline 17 April 2026, match early June 2026 (next cycle dates not yet posted); off-cycle January 2027 position open outside the match
f.International applicants: Institution policy: IMGs welcome to apply; must hold a valid ECFMG certificate and be able to obtain Medical Board of California licensure; non-ACGME fellowships need ACGME Non-Standard Training recognition before J-1 sponsorship
f.Visa support: Institution policy: J-1 (ECFMG) is the primary visa; H-1B permitted only in some circumstances with GME approval; O-1 rarely, varies by department
f.Funding: Institution policy: Paid on Stanford Health Care housestaff scale 2026-27: PGY4 $113,276.80, PGY5 $119,558.40, PGY6 $124,280.00, PGY7 $130,540.80 (base includes housing allowance)
f.Start: Not stated for match positions; an off-cycle position outside the match starts January 2027

t: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship
i: UCLA Health
su: Regional anaesthesia training in ultrasound-guided peripheral blocks, catheters, thoracic epidurals and acute pain service management, with clinical scholarship.

f.Deadline: 2027–28 cycle: applications opened 5 January 2026; deadline 4 March 2026 (closed). 2028–29 dates not yet posted
f.International applicants: IMGs may apply; valid ECFMG certificate and notarized English translations of diploma/transcripts required (ACGME-accredited anesthesiology residency still required)
f.Visa support: Not stated on official page
f.Funding: Salary not stated; fellows may work as attending staff 1–2 days/week for additional income

t: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship
i: UCSF Health
su: Regional anaesthesia and perioperative pain training across UCSF, Zuckerberg San Francisco General and Kaiser South San Francisco sites.

f.International applicants: Institution policy: IMGs eligible if their school is in the World Directory/FAIMER and they hold a valid ECFMG certificate at application; non-US citizens need permanent residence, an appropriate visa or DACA
f.Visa support: Institution policy: UCSF sponsors J-1 (ECFMG) and H-1B (incl. OPT) visas; H-1B/OPT require pre-approval by UCSF OGME; non-ACGME fellowships can take J-1 trainees only if ACGME Non-Standard Training (NST) recognised
f.Funding: Institution policy: Salaried on UCSF CIR collective-bargaining scale (rates effective 1 Oct 2025, incl. housing allowance): PGY4 $106,127; PGY5 $109,737; PGY6 $113,149; PGY7 $116,315; PGY8 $121,494; 2026-27 scale under union negotiation

t: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship
i: University of Pennsylvania (Penn Medicine)
su: A year-long fellowship across Penn Presbyterian (Level 1 trauma), HUP and an ambulatory centre performing about 5,400 blocks a year, with a dedicated acute pain service and part-time clinical instructorship.

f.International applicants: Not stated on official page
f.Visa support: Not stated on official page
f.Funding: Attending salary prorated to days worked as an instructor

t: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship
i: University of Pittsburgh / UPMC
su: A 12-month subspecialty programme in regional anesthesiology and acute pain medicine across UPMC hospitals, selecting up to 15 fellows a year.

f.Deadline: Applications accepted on a continual (rolling) basis
f.International applicants: Applicants from non-ACGME accredited anesthesiology residencies may apply with completion certificate and summative evaluation
f.Visa support: Institution policy: UPMC ME programmes may (not required to) offer J-1 via ECFMG and/or H-1B; programme can offer either or both; H-1B requires USMLE Steps 1-3 passed by match date
f.Funding: Institution policy: Salaried on UPMC ME GMT stipend scale AY 2026-27: PGY4 $78,677; PGY5 $81,431; PGY6 $84,281; PGY7 $87,231; PGY8 $90,284 (AY 2027-28: PGY4 $81,818; PGY5 $85,091; PGY6 $88,495)

t: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship
i: UT Southwestern Medical Center
su: A comprehensive ACGME-accredited 12-month programme in neuraxial, perineural, truncal and chest wall blocks and acute pain management at University and Parkland hospitals.

f.International applicants: Institution policy: IMGs must be ECFMG-certified and hold an ECFMG-sponsored J-1 visa for clinical training at UTSW
f.Visa support: Not currently accepting or sponsoring training visas
f.Funding: Institution policy: Paid house-staff stipend (employer varies: UTSW, Parkland, Children's Health or Scottish Rite); 2026-27 scale PGY4 $82,225, PGY5 $86,343, PGY6 $89,505, PGY7 $95,050

t: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship
i: Weill Cornell Medicine / NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital
su: An ACGME-accredited 12-month fellowship on a service performing over 3,000 blocks a year, with rotations at NYP/Weill Cornell, the David H. Koch ambulatory centre, NYP/Columbia and Memorial Sloan Kettering.

f.International applicants: Institution policy: Foreign nationals accepted only if they secure ECFMG J-1 status or hold work authorization for the programme duration; IMGs need ECFMG certification
f.Visa support: NewYork-Presbyterian accepts only J-1 visas for ACGME fellowship programmes in the Department of Anesthesiology
f.Funding: Salary $113,500 (2024–25); $900 book allowance; $2,000 conference reimbursement
f.Start: Institution policy: NYP graduate staff appointment year is generally 1 July - 30 June

t: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship (Florida)
i: Mayo Clinic — Florida
su: Training combines ultrasound-guided regional techniques, continuous catheters, acute pain care and resident supervision.

f.Deadline: Applications via SF Match January-March of the year preceding start
f.International applicants: Not stated on official page
f.Visa support: J-1 via ECFMG sponsorship; Mayo Clinic may also sponsor H-1B if all eligibility requirements are met
f.Funding: Paid; Mayo Clinic GME stipend by graduate level (effective 11 March 2026: e.g. Graduate Level 5 $89,036/yr); benefits include 20 working days' vacation

t: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship (Minnesota)
i: Mayo Clinic — Minnesota
su: A regional anesthesia and acute pain fellowship supported by Mayo's clinical, research and educational resources.

f.Deadline: Applications open January; all materials due 1 May of the year preceding the start date; interviews 1 Feb-30 May
f.International applicants: Yes - graduates of non-US medical schools eligible if ECFMG-certified before appointment (or hold a full unrestricted US licence in the program state)
f.Visa support: ECFMG J-1 sponsorship supported; H-1B only where it can be obtained by change/extension of status without the new $100,000 petition payment
f.Funding: Paid stipend; Mayo Clinic GME annual stipend equivalents (effective 11 March 2026) range from $75,105 to $106,096 by training level, plus benefits incl. 20 days vacation

t: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship at Mount Sinai West and Mount Sinai Morningside
i: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
su: A one-year programme across an orthopedic-centric hospital and a Level II trauma centre, training academic and clinical leaders in regional anesthesiology with trauma, truncal, POCUS and pediatric regional rotations.

f.International applicants: Institution policy: IMGs accepted with valid ECFMG certificate; may not begin training until an appropriate visa is obtained
f.Visa support: Institution policy: Mount Sinai Health System offers J-1 (ECFMG) and H-1B (categorical candidates in programmes of 2+ years, ECFMG-certified with USMLE Step 3 passed by Match) plus E-3 for Australians; programme director decides which is offered
f.Funding: Institution policy: ACGME fellows paid by PGY level (Mount Sinai Hospital stipend effective January 2026: PGY4 $106,313, PGY5 $110,565); non-ACGME fellow pay set by programme funds

t: Regional Anesthesiology and Acute Pain Medicine Fellowship at The Mount Sinai Hospital
i: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
su: A one-year ACGME-accredited fellowship providing advanced regional anesthesia training through extensive clinical work, teaching and research, including dedicated block-fellow supervision days.

f.International applicants: Exceptionally qualified international graduates with ECFMG certification may be approved
f.Visa support: Institution policy: Mount Sinai Health System offers J-1 (ECFMG) and H-1B (categorical candidates in programmes of 2+ years, ECFMG-certified with USMLE Step 3 passed by Match) plus E-3 for Australians; programme director decides which is offered
f.Funding: Institution policy: ACGME fellows paid by PGY level (Mount Sinai Hospital stipend effective January 2026: PGY4 $106,313, PGY5 $110,565); non-ACGME fellow pay set by programme funds

i: University of Washington
su: Regional anaesthesia and acute pain training across UW and Harborview, including ultrasound-guided blocks, catheters and inpatient and ambulatory services.

f.Deadline: Rolling – applications accepted on an ongoing basis
f.International applicants: Yes – ECFMG documentation and citizenship-status documentation (if applicable) required
f.Visa support: Institution policy: J-1 sponsored by ECFMG (ACGME programmes and non-ACGME programmes approved as ACGME non-standard training); H-1B only with prior GME Office (and ISO) approval before ranking/offer, for limited eligibility categories and requires USMLE Step 3; F-1 OPT accepted; no O-1 or permanent-residence sponsorship
f.Funding: Paid per UW GME salary schedule; academic allowance; internal moonlighting may be approved. Fellows work 40% as Acting Instructor

i: McGill University
su: A one-year clinical fellowship in anaesthesia for robotic oncological surgery.

f.Deadline: 2027–2028 applications opened 15 May 2026; deadline for most fellowships 1 September 2026 (see PGME Application Timelines)
f.International applicants: Yes — Regular Track positions open to Canadian and international applicants; French language training mandatory for fellows with no or limited conversational French
f.Visa support: Not stated on official page
f.Funding: Candidates must secure funding in order to apply; self-funding not accepted; Quebec-trained residents may apply for RAMQ-funded fellowships

i: College of Anaesthesiologists of Ireland
su: An optional, competitively allocated seventh year of Specialist Anaesthesiology Training in a subspecialty, leading to a CAI Certificate of Fellowship in addition to the CSCST.

f.Deadline: Positions commencing July 2025 closed; future rounds not stated
f.International applicants: No — restricted to holders of a CSCST from the College of Anaesthesiologists of Ireland
f.Visa support: Not applicable (Irish CSCST holders)
f.Funding: SpR salary for the duration of the fellowship (HSE NDTP-funded)

t: Senior Clinical Fellow in Anaesthesia for HPB and Liver Transplantation
i: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
o: King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
su: A combined post giving senior trainees or qualified anaesthetists experience in adult and paediatric anaesthesia for liver transplantation, hepatobiliary surgery and imaging procedures.

f.Deadline: Recruited via periodic NHS Jobs adverts; most recent advert closed
f.International applicants: Yes — applicants requiring Skilled Worker visa sponsorship considered
f.Visa support: Skilled Worker sponsorship applicants welcome and considered alongside all other applications (per NHS Jobs advert)
f.Funding: Salaried: £55,329–£63,152 per annum including London Zone (2025 advert)

t: Senior Clinical Fellow in Cardiothoracic Anaesthesia
i: Harefield Hospital (Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust)
o: Harefield Hospital (Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust)
su: Modular experience in adult cardiac surgery, thoracic surgery and cardiothoracic intensive care anaesthesia at Harefield, with opportunities for research and TOE skills.

f.Deadline: Recruited via periodic NHS Jobs adverts; most recent advert closed
f.International applicants: Yes — applicants requiring Skilled Worker visa sponsorship considered
f.Visa support: Skilled Worker sponsorship applicants welcome and considered alongside all other applications (per NHS Jobs advert)
f.Funding: Not stated on official page

t: Senior Clinical Fellow in Paediatric Anaesthesia
i: Evelina London Children's Hospital (Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust)
o: Evelina London Children's Hospital (Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust)
su: Tertiary paediatric anaesthesia experience across all surgical specialties except neurosurgery and liver transplantation, including high-volume neonatal surgery and paediatric cardiac anaesthesia.

f.Deadline: Recruited via periodic NHS Jobs adverts; most recent advert closed (closed 7 April 2026)
f.International applicants: Yes — applicants requiring Skilled Worker visa sponsorship considered
f.Visa support: Skilled Worker sponsorship applicants welcome and considered alongside all other applications (per NHS Jobs advert)
f.Funding: Salaried: £73,992 per annum (2026 advert)

i: Fiona Stanley Fremantle Hospitals Group
su: Trains fellows to design, run and debrief in-situ multidisciplinary simulation scenarios and coordinate ANZCA-approved courses such as CICO and cardiac arrest updates.

f.Deadline: Recruitment yearly via MedCareersWA; formal recruitment pool opens approximately March/April; roles may also arise during the year
f.International applicants: Yes — fellowship positions are open to local and international candidates
f.Visa support: Institution policy: Applicants must be eligible to work in Australia; those requiring visa sponsorship indicate this in their MedCareersWA application
f.Funding: Salaried per WA Health System – Medical Practitioners – AMA Industrial Agreement 2022, with salary packaging

i: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
o: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
su: A structured head-and-neck and advanced-airway fellowship combining complex clinical cases, simulation, teaching and research.

f.International applicants: Yes - overseas applicants via RCoA Medical Training Initiative (MTI) or Tier 2/Skilled Worker sponsorship
f.Visa support: MTI route: Tier 5 visa with Certificate of Sponsorship from the Academy of Medical Royal Colleges; or Tier 2/Skilled Worker CoS from OUH
f.Funding: Not stated on official page

t: Sleep, Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine (SleAP) Fellowship
i: Toronto Western Hospital & Women's College Hospital
su: Combines clinical anaesthesia with research at the Sleep, Anesthesia and Pain Medicine Research Unit, the first clinical-research centre focused on sleep disruption in perioperative and chronic pain settings.

f.International applicants: Yes — University of Toronto fellowships accept international graduates; English proficiency required where training was not in English
f.Visa support: Institution policy: international clinical fellows need an IRCC work permit; the PGME Office issues an LMIA-exempt offer of employment number and supports the work permit application
f.Funding: Institution policy: clinical fellows must be funded (department or sponsoring agency); FEAC recommends pay at least equal to PGY1 on the PARO salary scale, and foreign nationals must be paid at a rate commensurate with a Canadian in the same role

t: T32 Clinician Scientist Training in Perioperative Science Fellowship
i: Vanderbilt University Medical Center
su: An NIGMS T32 programme preparing basic and physician scientists to optimise perioperative care through mentored research training with protected research time.

f.Positions: Two to three new trainees per year (maximum 6 participants)
f.International applicants: Institution policy: Foreign medical graduates eligible with a valid ECFMG certificate (or full unrestricted Tennessee licence); programme-specific requirements also apply
f.Visa support: Institution policy: J-1 via ECFMG; H-1B considered case by case by programme with GME; no new O-1 applications supported
f.Funding: NIGMS T32 funded

i: University of Washington
su: Postdoctoral training supports research careers across anesthesiology and perioperative medicine, spanning biomedical, clinical, population and health-services approaches.

f.Duration: At least 2 years; extension to a third year is possible
f.Deadline: Application deadline for the latest posted cycle: 28 February 2026
f.International applicants: Not eligible: US citizens or permanent residents only (NIH regulations)
f.Visa support: None: US citizenship or permanent residency required
f.Funding: NIH training-grant salary uses the NIH scale according to prior training.

t: T32 Research Fellowship — Research in Anesthesia Training Program (ReAP)
i: Stanford Medicine
su: An NIH-funded T32 programme that trains future leaders in academic anesthesia through mentored research in neuroscience/pain, injury/inflammation/immunity, and outcomes research/bioinformatics.

f.Duration: Two-year training experiences anticipated for most candidates
f.Deadline: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
f.Positions: Four trainees in total, two appointed per year
f.International applicants: Individuals on temporary or student visas are not eligible
f.Visa support: Not eligible on temporary visas; post-residency fellowship programme does not sponsor H1B visas and J1 applicants are not eligible
f.Funding: NIH T32 funded
f.Start: Institution policy: Stanford GME contracts are issued per academic year (1 July - 30 June); standard start late June/1 July

i: Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
o: Royal Papworth Hospital NHS Foundation Trust
su: A 6-month fellowship in advanced thoracic anaesthesia, lung transplant anaesthesia and ECMO, including robotic and minimally invasive thoracic surgery at the UK's leading heart and lung hospital.

f.Deadline: Recruited via periodic NHS Jobs adverts; most recent advert closed
f.International applicants: Yes — applicants requiring Skilled Worker visa sponsorship considered
f.Visa support: Skilled Worker sponsorship applicants welcome and considered alongside all other applications (per NHS Jobs advert)
f.Funding: Salaried: £73,992 per annum (2025 advert)

i: Mass General Brigham
su: Focused thoracic anesthesia training spans Massachusetts General and Brigham and Women's, with lung isolation, advanced airway and transplant experience.

f.Duration: 12 months, individualized to experience and goals
f.International applicants: Visa sponsorship (H-1B and J-1) available; no other international-applicant criteria stated
f.Visa support: The official page states institutional sponsorship of H-1B and J-1 visas.
f.Funding: Paid; starting salary for PGY-5 in 2025 is $99,967 plus health, dental, disability and other insurance

i: Toronto General Hospital (University Health Network)
su: Thoracic anaesthesia fellowship emphasising care of patients with end-stage lung disease, including approximately 200 lung transplants and 60–70 pulmonary endarterectomies per year.

f.Deadline: Applications open 24 months and close 12 months before the intended start date
f.International applicants: Yes — applicants trained in countries where English is not the primary language must demonstrate effective communication in English
f.Visa support: Institution policy: international clinical fellows need an IRCC work permit; the PGME Office issues an LMIA-exempt offer of employment number and supports the work permit application
f.Funding: Institution policy: clinical fellows must be funded (department or sponsoring agency); FEAC recommends pay at least equal to PGY1 on the PARO salary scale, and foreign nationals must be paid at a rate commensurate with a Canadian in the same role
f.Start: Normally beginning of February and beginning of August each year

i: UCLA Health
su: Advanced thoracic anesthesia training focuses on high-acuity chest surgery in adults and children, including lung transplantation and complex oncological procedures.

f.Deadline: No deadline (rolling review once file complete)
f.International applicants: IMGs may apply; Medical Board of California Applicant Evaluation Status Letter required
f.Visa support: Institution policy (UCLA GME, ACGME programmes): ECFMG-sponsored clinical J-1 is the preferred visa; H-1B considered only for US LCME/AOA graduates moving from F-1 OPT, trainees already in clinical training on H-1B with enough time left, or physicians of national/international renown (department-funded, case by case)
f.Funding: Institution policy (UCLA ACGME residents/fellows, CIR-SEIU contract): from 1 Sept 2026 PGY4 $108,102; PGY5 $111,894; PGY6 $115,477; PGY7 $118,801; PGY8 $124,242 (PGY1 $98,466); rising from 1 July 2027 (PGY4 $113,508); plus $8,000/yr Resident Enhancement Fund

i: Yale School of Medicine / Yale New Haven Hospital
su: A thoracic anesthesiology fellowship with three clinical days weekly in thoracic ORs, one attending day in general ORs, interventional pulmonology time and no overnight or weekend call commitment.

f.International applicants: Institution policy: Foreign medical graduates accepted into accredited residencies/fellowships; J-1 requires valid ECFMG certificate and Ministry of Health statement of need
f.Visa support: Institution policy: YNHH/YSM GME accepts foreign nationals on J-1 (ECFMG-sponsored), F-1, or H-1B transfers from a current programme
f.Funding: Includes one day weekly as an attending anesthesiologist in general ORs

i: Toronto General Hospital (University Health Network)
su: A 6- to 12-month fellowship in comprehensive pain management across the Transitional Pain Service Clinic, MSK clinics and the Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome Program.

f.Deadline: January 2027 intake closes 1 October 2026; July 2027 closes 1 April 2027; later intakes through July 2029 open
f.International applicants: Yes — applicants trained in countries where English is not the primary language must demonstrate effective communication in English
f.Visa support: Institution policy: international clinical fellows need an IRCC work permit; the PGME Office issues an LMIA-exempt offer of employment number and supports the work permit application
f.Funding: Institution policy: clinical fellows must be funded (department or sponsoring agency); FEAC recommends pay at least equal to PGY1 on the PARO salary scale, and foreign nationals must be paid at a rate commensurate with a Canadian in the same role

i: Columbia University Irving Medical Center
su: Combined clinical and research training concentrates on liver transplantation and major vascular surgery, with a clinical–research balance tailored to the fellow's academic plans.

f.Duration: 1 or 2 years (combined liver transplantation and major vascular anesthesiology fellowship)
f.International applicants: Possible if eligible for US employment; ECFMG certificate required where applicable
f.Visa support: No H-1B sponsorship: NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital and Columbia University do not sponsor H-1B visas for GME
f.Funding: Institution policy: NewYork-Presbyterian 2026-27 house-staff salary PGY1 $96,600; PGY2 $107,000; PGY3 $115,700; PGY4 $119,100; PGY5 $123,000; PGY6 $125,200; PGY7 $129,100, plus $7,500 living supplement, $1,000 academic stipend, $2,000 Lyft credit and $2,160 meal stipend

i: Cleveland Clinic
su: Clinical training covers liver, intestinal and multivisceral transplantation, complex hepatobiliary procedures and combined cardiac–liver cases.

f.International applicants: Yes
f.Visa support: Cleveland Clinic GME supports H-1B and J-1 (ECFMG-sponsored) for GME trainees; programme-specific policy not stated
f.Funding: Paid position (salary amount not stated); institutional funding up to $2,500 to present at a conference, $1,000 educational expenses, $60/month on-call meal allowance, 20 paid days off

i: Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre
su: Develops expertise in managing trauma during initial triage, intra- and post-operative care, including training in the Trauma Team Leader role at the largest trauma centre in Canada.

f.Duration: 12 months (shorter or longer may be pursued under certain circumstances)
f.Deadline: Apply at least 15 months in advance; online forms open for July 2027, July 2028 and July 2029 intakes
f.International applicants: Yes — open to international graduates; applicants whose first language is not English must pass TOEFL/TSE or IELTS
f.Visa support: Not stated on official page
f.Funding: Not stated on official page

i: The Alfred, Bayside Health
su: Training in trauma evaluation, resuscitation and anaesthesia across emergency and elective trauma surgery.

f.Deadline: 31 May 2026 for 2027 intake (advertised 4-31 May 2026; applications now closed); next cycle not yet posted
f.International applicants: Accepted; international applicants should be at or near the end of specialty training, with relevant postgraduate exams passed at time of application
f.Visa support: Institution policy: Employer-sponsored Training visa (subclass 407) is Alfred Health's preferred visa for IMGs (granted 13 months); Medical Workforce team supports visa nomination, starting at least 6 months before commencement
f.Funding: Not stated on official page

t: Trauma and Acute Care Surgery Anesthesia Clinical Instructor Program
i: UCSF Health
su: A 12-month UCSF/ZSFG programme preparing anesthesiologists to lead in trauma and acute care anesthesia, combining attending work with supervised trauma call, research or QI projects, POCUS/echo training and teaching.

f.International applicants: Institution policy: IMGs eligible if their school is in the World Directory/FAIMER and they hold a valid ECFMG certificate at application; non-US citizens need permanent residence, an appropriate visa or DACA
f.Visa support: Institution policy: UCSF sponsors J-1 (ECFMG) and H-1B (incl. OPT) visas; H-1B/OPT require pre-approval by UCSF OGME; non-ACGME fellowships can take J-1 trainees only if ACGME Non-Standard Training (NST) recognised
f.Funding: Employed by UCSF; average of three days per week as an attending anesthesiologist; department-funded ECO 1 echo course, ATLS and conference attendance

i: University of Washington
su: Harborview-based training spans perioperative trauma care, resuscitation and trauma analgesia, with 60% fellowship time and 40% faculty work.

f.Duration: 12 months; two additional orientation months are recommended for fellows new to US practice
f.International applicants: Accepted: foreign graduates need a WHO-listed medical school, completed anesthesiology residency and unrestricted home-country licence; USMLE 1-3 and ECFMG documentation required
f.Visa support: H-1B sponsorship may be offered in limited, exceptional cases for highly qualified candidates.
f.Funding: Competitive faculty-fellowship salary (60% fellowship / 40% faculty time)
f.Start: Any point in the academic year; most fellows start between July and September

i: Washington University in St. Louis (WashU Medicine)
su: One of only a few U.S. trauma anesthesiology fellowships, with seven months on the Trauma Anesthesia Service plus ICU and elective rotations, averaging 16 shifts a month.

f.International applicants: Residency abroad accepted with USMLE passed
f.Visa support: Accepts a variety of visas but cannot sponsor new H-1 visa applications at this time; applicants already on H-1B may be considered
f.Funding: Institution policy: WashU/BJH/SLCH GME Consortium stipends 1 July 2026-30 June 2027: PGY1 $71,239; PGY2 $74,399; PGY3 $77,597; PGY4 $80,895; PGY5 $84,439; PGY6 $88,091; PGY7 $91,618; PGY8 $95,032; PGY9 $99,151 (all fellows paid PGY-based salary whether or not ACGME-accredited)

t: Trauma, Neuroanesthesia and Critical Care Fellowship
i: St. Michael's Hospital (Unity Health Toronto)
su: Neuroanaesthesia, trauma and neurocritical care training at a Level 1 Trauma Centre and major provincial referral centre for neurological and neurosurgical disease.

f.International applicants: Yes — University of Toronto fellowships accept international graduates; English proficiency required where training was not in English
f.Visa support: Institution policy: international clinical fellows need an IRCC work permit; the PGME Office issues an LMIA-exempt offer of employment number and supports the work permit application
f.Funding: Institution policy: clinical fellows must be funded (department or sponsoring agency); FEAC recommends pay at least equal to PGY1 on the PARO salary scale, and foreign nationals must be paid at a rate commensurate with a Canadian in the same role
f.Start: Institution policy: University of Toronto PGME academic year runs 1 July - 30 June (letters of appointment issued per academic year; off-cycle starts possible)

i: Weill Cornell Medicine / NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital
su: A 12-month ACGME-accredited interventional pain medicine programme with core rotations at NewYork-Presbyterian/Weill Cornell, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and Hospital for Special Surgery.

f.Deadline: ERAS applications accepted 3 December 2025 – 31 March 2026 (current cycle)
f.International applicants: Institution policy: Foreign nationals accepted only if they secure ECFMG J-1 status or hold work authorization for the programme duration; IMGs need ECFMG certification
f.Visa support: NewYork-Presbyterian accepts only J-1 visas for ACGME fellowship programmes in the Department of Anesthesiology
f.Funding: Institution policy: NYPH 2026-27 GME salary: PGY4 $119,100, PGY5 $123,000, PGY6 $125,200, PGY7 $129,100, plus $7,500 living supplement, $1,000 academic stipend, Lyft and meal credits
f.Start: Institution policy: NYP graduate staff appointment year is generally 1 July - 30 June

t: Trust Clinical Fellow in Education and Anaesthesia

F-1 OPT accepted for first year for US-school graduates
